  · rintro ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩

findings.problem: The equality of the two images is proved by a manual `ext z` double-inclusion. This repeats the pointwise identification of `schwarzChristoffelBoundary` with `L` in both directions and requires a `.symm` rewrite in the first branch, although the only mathematical input is that the two functions agree on `Ioo p q`.
findings.proposed_change:
Replace the `convert`/`ext`/`constructor` block with an explicit image-congruence step:

```lean
  obtain ⟨L, hL, -, -, hLcol⟩ :=
    exists_tendsto_schwarzChristoffelPrimitive_injOn_collinear a e z₀ ha
  have himg : schwarzChristoffelBoundary a e z₀ '' Ioo p q = L '' Ioo p q :=
    Set.image_congr fun x hx =>
      schwarzChristoffelBoundary_eq_of_tendsto a e z₀ x (hL x hx)
  rwa [himg]
```

This uses the existing lemma `Set.image_congr`; the empty-interval case is handled by the same equality of images.
findings.benefit: The proof now states the key idea directly: the images agree because the boundary map and the local limit function `L` agree on every point of `Ioo p q`. It removes the manual membership argument and the `.symm` bookkeeping, while keeping the dependence on `hL` fully visible.

      (ContinuousAt.stronglyMeasurableAtFilter isOpen_Ioo
        (fun y hy ↦ (hdcontOn y hy).continuousAt (isOpen_Ioo.mem_nhds hy)) x hx) hdcont
findings.problem: The measurability side condition for the fundamental theorem of calculus is discharged by re-deriving pointwise continuity from `hdcontOn` and then applying `ContinuousAt.stronglyMeasurableAtFilter`. This wraps a standard implication `ContinuousOn → StronglyMeasurableAtFilter` in an auxiliary pointwise function, obscuring the fact that continuity of the density on `Ioo p q` is the only input needed.
findings.proposed_change:
Use the `ContinuousOn` form of the same Mathlib lemma directly:

```lean
    intervalIntegral.integral_hasDerivAt_right (by simp)
      (hdcontOn.stronglyMeasurableAtFilter isOpen_Ioo x hx) hdcont
```

The `ContinuousOn.stronglyMeasurableAtFilter` lemma is already available in the imported Mathlib files; the same dot-notation pattern appears in TauCeti's `Rigidity.lean`.
findings.benefit: The FTC application becomes a three-line, direct use of `hdcontOn` as a strong measurability hypothesis. A reader no longer has to check an auxiliary function `fun y hy => ...` that merely repackages continuity already known on the whole interval.

evidence.excerpt:
theorem ContinuousOn.stronglyMeasurableAtFilter [TopologicalSpace α] [OpensMeasurableSpace α]
    [TopologicalSpace β] [PseudoMetrizableSpace β] [SecondCountableTopologyEither α β] {f : α → β}
    {s : Set α} {μ : Measure α} (hs : IsOpen s) (hf : ContinuousOn f s) :
    ∀ x ∈ s, StronglyMeasurableAtFilter f (𝓝 x) μ := fun _x hx =>
  ⟨s, IsOpen.mem_nhds hs hx, hf.aestronglyMeasurable hs.measurableSet⟩

findings.problem: The proof introduces a particular boundary limit function `L` and its continuity from `exists_tendsto_schwarzChristoffelPrimitive_sub_eq`, even though the general theorem `continuousOn_schwarzChristoffelBoundary_of_exponent_sum_gt_neg_one` is already available. On `Ioo p q`, its exponent-sum hypothesis is exactly supplied by `sum_filter_eq_zero_of_mem_Ioo`, the helper defined earlier in this file.
findings.proposed_change:
Replace the extraction of `L` with a direct application of the general continuity criterion:

```lean
  refine continuousOn_schwarzChristoffelBoundary_of_exponent_sum_gt_neg_one a e z₀ fun x hx => ?_
  rw [sum_filter_eq_zero_of_mem_Ioo a e ha hx]
  norm_num
```

This is the same pattern used by `continuousOn_schwarzChristoffelBoundary_Icc` later in the file and by `SeparatedEdge.lean` when deriving the inequality `-1 < ∑ i with a i = x, e i`.
findings.benefit: The open-interval statement becomes a short corollary of the named exponent-sum continuity theorem, with no auxiliary function `L` or `hLcont` to follow. It also makes the relationship between the open-interval and closed-interval continuity results explicit and avoids duplicating the boundary-limit machinery in this declaration.
